title: Customers redirected to cloned checkout that captures card details — anyone else affected?
text: We’re investigating customer reports of an external checkout redirect affecting three of our Shopify stores. Customers are taken to checkout-guard[.]top , where a counterfeit checkout displays their actual basket. We’ve retrieved its client-side source code, which is designed to collect card and billing details, display a payment error, then redirect the customer back to the genuine Shopify checkout to complete payment. This means resulting orders can look normal in Shopify admin. We’ve reported our findings to Shopify and contacted our app providers. We haven’t yet established how the redirect is being triggered and haven’t reliably reproduced it ourselves. Has anyone else encountered this domain or behaviour, or identified the source of a similar redirect? The counterfeit checkout’s code includes the distinctive misspellings “CHECKIOUT” and “checkiout”. We also found references to “Vitamin A Swim” in the counterfeit checkout’s source code, including sourceId: "vitaminaswim-clone" , copied branding/legal text and a Shopify address-autocomplete endpoint associated with shop ID 26687963179 . This suggests the fake checkout uses a cloned swimwear-store template. It does not establish that Vitamin A Swim is involved in the attack. We’ve shared the endpoint details privately with Shopify. Please don’t post customer information or payment details here. Any technical findings that could help connect the incidents would be appreciated. 7 posts - 5 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchants investigating fraudulent external checkout redirect scam.

title: How often do you sync supplier stock with your Shopify store?
text: I run a small dropshipping store and built an automation that syncs supplier stock to Shopify every 4 hours. It works, but I still worry about the gap: an item can sell out at the supplier between syncs and a customer can still order it. For those of you with supplier-based inventory: How often do you sync? Do you keep a safety buffer (for example, showing 0 when the supplier has fewer than 5)? How do you handle the occasional order for something that’s actually gone? Curious what’s worked for others. 9 posts - 5 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Dropshipper dealing with inventory sync timing gaps and overselling.

title: Sell Master Carton (5 Sets + Carton) as one item & auto-deduct packing without Product Bundle (v16)
text: Hello everyone, Version details: Frappe Framework: v16.51.0 (version-16) ERPNext: v16.50.0 (version-16) India Compliance: v16.10.1 (version-16) Frappe CRM: v2.0.0-dev (develop) Business scenario: We manufacture tool sets. For dispatch, we pack 5 finished sets into one 7ply master carton and sell it to the customer as one unit: “Excel P14 Master Carton - 5 Sets”. Components per master carton: P14 Set x 5 (finished stock item) 7ply Master Carton x 1 (packing material, stock item) Requirements: In Sales Order and Sales Invoice, the customer should see only ONE line item (Master Carton with description and price). Stock of the 5 sets + 1 packing carton must be deducted automatically. We do NOT want to use Product Bundle, because it creates a Packed Items table and we don’t want to depend on “Print Hide” settings. We do NOT use Pick List or Packing Slip. What we tried: Product Bundle: works for stock deduction, but the component items (Packed Items) appear on the Sales Order / Invoice, exposing our internal packing breakdown. Options we are considering: A) Make the Master Carton a stock item with a BOM (5 Sets + 1 Carton) and use Stock Entry (Manufacture / Repack) when packing. Then sell the Master Carton item directly. B) Sell the P14 Set with a sales UOM “Master Carton” (conversion factor 5), but then the packing carton is not deducted automatically. Questions: Is Option A (BOM + Repack/Manufacture Stock Entry) the recommended approach in v16 for this packing scenario? Should we use Stock Entry type “Manufacture” or “Repack” here? Which one handles valuation (sets + carton cost) better? Is there any standard way in v16 to auto-deduct packing material on Delivery Note without Product Bundle or custom scripts? Any best practice from others with a similar packing-material flow? Screenshots attached: Item master, BOM, Sales Order. Thank you! 2 posts - 2 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: ERPNext user needing to sell master carton bundles and auto-deduct packing materials.
